Check a running model

Is Ollama Using My GPU?

Send a short request to a local model, then run ollama ps on the same server. The PROCESSOR column reports where Ollama loaded that model. 100% GPU indicates full GPU placement, 100% CPU indicates CPU placement, and a CPU/GPU split indicates both. Use the server log to confirm the backend and the actual offloaded layers.

  1. Get a loaded-model reading
  2. Choose the next check
  3. Troubleshoot CPU or mixed placement
  4. Interpret a 100% GPU reading
  5. Compare the three measured runs

Get a loaded-model reading

Use ollama list to pick an installed local chat model. Replace the example tag with that exact name. Run the request against the server you want to check, then inspect it before the two-minute keep-alive expires.

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen2.5:0.5b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK and nothing else."}],"options":{"num_ctx":4096,"num_predict":24,"temperature":0},"stream":false,"keep_alive":"2m"}'

ollama ps

Check that the CLI points to the same host and port as the request. If the list is empty, a model may have unloaded, the request may have failed or the CLI may be looking at another server. Read the response first, then check the same server again. For an API view of the running list, request /api/ps.

What does ollama ps report?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Ollama reports 100% CPU or a CPU/GPU split

  1. Look for the backend in the server log. If it does not list the expected GPU, verify hardware and driver support on the system running Ollama. In a container, check that the Ollama process has access to the device. On Apple Silicon, test the native app or binary and look for Metal.
  2. Check for a forced CPU or layer limit. In our llamacpp run, options.num_gpu: 0 produced 100% CPU even though the server detected Metal. Review overrides in the client request, model or server. Start an automatic-placement check with a freshly loaded model.
  3. Try a smaller load if the GPU is detected. Keep one local model loaded for the comparison. Try a smaller model or reduce context length, then confirm the actual loaded context and processor. See how to verify Ollama context length.

On macOS, app logs are in ~/.ollama/logs/server.log. On systemd Linux use journalctl -u ollama. For Windows and container paths, see the Ollama log guide. Use the log belonging to the service that answered your request.

What 100% GPU means in ollama ps

The processor percentage describes reported placement. For current activity or performance, sample GPU activity while a request is running and measure tokens generated per second separately. A model can remain GPU-loaded and sit idle between requests.

/api/ps reports size and size_vram in bytes. Compare the corresponding model row. In our partial run, the API reported about 37% of the loaded size on the GPU, while the log reported 5 of 25 layers offloaded. Layers have different sizes, and Apple Silicon uses unified memory.

After checking CPU and GPU placement, measure generation speed and model load time separately with a repeatable local request.

Three readings from the same model and context

On November 28, 2026 we used Ollama 0.40.18, the llamacpp runner and one Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M GGUF on an Apple M4. We unloaded between runs, kept the context at 4,096 and used the same short prompt. Each request returned LOCAL_OK.
